analysis.time: The event occurred in May 2026, with the report published on July 17, 2026. The case is part of a broader surveillance period from 1993 to the end of 2023.
analysis.location_and_population: Douglas County, Colorado, United States. The affected population includes an adult and 41 people under monitoring for hantavirus in connection to the cruise ship outbreak.
analysis.event: A confirmed death from hantavirus in Colorado, reported by USA TODAY and the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment. The case is not linked to the recent cruise ship outbreak.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: One confirmed death in Colorado. There are 41 people under monitoring for hantavirus in connection to the cruise ship outbreak. The disease is rare, with around one to two dozen cases reported annually in the U.S. The risk to the general public remains low.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Health officials have confirmed the case is not connected to the cruise ship outbreak. The CDC has been conducting surveillance since 1993. The virus is primarily carried by wild rodents, and infection occurs through inhalation of particles from rodent waste.

title: Manifold’s Hondius Hantavirus Market: Why Bettors Put Just 2% on a Non-Passenger Case - tech-insider.org

analysis.time: The outbreak was identified in April 2026, the WHO declared it over on July 2, 2026, and the Manifold market was published on July 15, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The event concerns the MV Hondius cruise ship outbreak, which affected passengers and crew, and the market focuses on the potential for secondary transmission to non-passengers such as ground staff or family members.
analysis.event: A Manifold prediction market asked whether at least one non-passenger would catch hantavirus from the MV Hondius outbreak. The market is a binary contract hosted on Manifold, and the WHO declared the outbreak over on July 2, 2026.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak resulted in 13 cases and three deaths, with a case fatality ratio near 23%. The market reflects a crowd-implied probability of approximately 2% that a non-passenger will be infected, indicating a low but non-zero risk of secondary transmission.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The WHO declared the outbreak over on July 2, 2026, after the last close contact completed quarantine. The market remains active due to definitional ambiguity over 'non-passenger' and resolution timing incentives, with 145 unique bettors engaging in the same window.

analysis.brief_en: A Manifold prediction market priced the probability of a non-passenger contracting hantavirus from the MV Hondius outbreak at roughly 2% as of July 15, 2026. The market reflects the WHO's declaration that the outbreak ended on July 2, 2026, after 13 cases and three deaths. Traders are debating the definition of 'non-passenger,' with some interpreting it to include crew members, while the crowd appears to focus on secondary spread to people who never boarded the ship. The market remains active due to definitional ambiguity and resolution timing incentives, with 145 unique bettors engaging in the same window.
analysis.summary_en: A Manifold prediction market priced the probability of a non-passenger contracting hantavirus from the MV Hondius outbreak at roughly 2% as of July 15, 2026. The market reflects the WHO's declaration that the outbreak ended on July 2, 2026, after 13 cases and three deaths. title: MRNA Stock Closes Down On Profit-Taking Following 20% Weekly Rally And Hantavirus Buzz - Stocktwits

analysis.time: The news report was published on July 17, 2026. The event of the American citizen's diagnosis occurred on Sunday, July 15, 2026, and the stock market reaction took place on Monday, July 16, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: United States; the affected population includes an American citizen diagnosed with the Andes strain of hantavirus, who was repatriated from the MV Hondius cruise ship; the stock market reaction involves Moderna (MRNA) and its investors.
analysis.event: An American citizen was diagnosed with the Andes strain of hantavirus, and Moderna (MRNA) shares experienced a decline on Monday following a 20% weekly rally, attributed to profit-taking by investors. Moderna confirmed it is pursuing early-stage research into mRNA-based hantavirus vaccines.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The stock closed down 3% on Monday. The diagnosed citizen was asymptomatic and was transported in a biocontainment unit for monitoring. A second American on the same flight showed mild symptoms but was not yet confirmed positive. No hantavirus vaccine is currently approved, and human clinical trials for Moderna's candidates have not begun.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: health officials are monitoring the case. The asymptomatic passenger was transported to the University of Nebraska Medical Center’s biocontainment facility. Moderna is conducting preclinical work with USAMRIID and partnering with Korea University. The stock market reaction is attributed to profit-taking, and retail sentiment on Stocktwits shifted to 'extremely bullish'.

analysis.brief_en: Shares of Moderna (MRNA) fell 3% on Monday after a 20% weekly rally, likely due to profit-taking by investors. The decline followed news that an American citizen was diagnosed with the Andes strain of hantavirus, for which Moderna is reportedly developing a vaccine. The asymptomatic passenger was repatriated from the MV Hondius cruise ship and transported to a biocontainment facility in Nebraska for monitoring. Moderna confirmed it is pursuing early-stage mRNA-based hantavirus vaccine research, though no vaccine is currently approved and clinical trials have not begun. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits became 'extremely bullish' following the news.

title: Six hantavirus cruise passengers head to Australia - WFMZ.com

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-15. Event date: 2026-05-14 (flight departure); arrival expected 2026-05-15.
analysis.location_and_population: Australia (Perth, Western Australia); Netherlands (departure); cruise origin not specified.
analysis.event: Six hantavirus-exposed cruise passengers (four Australians, one Briton, one New Zealander) are being repatriated to Australia under official quarantine arrangements. Reported by the Australian government via Health Minister Mark Butler.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Six passengers, all asymptomatic, tested negative for hantavirus. No cases or deaths reported. Risk of transmission during flight mitigated by full PPE; incubation period up to 42 days noted.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Australian government arranged a dedicated plane with PPE for passengers; arrival at Perth air force base adjacent to a 500-bed quarantine facility for at least three weeks. analysis.brief_en: Australia is repatriating six hantavirus-exposed cruise passengers from the Netherlands on 14 May 2026, arriving in Perth the next day. All six—four Australians, one Briton, and one New Zealander—are asymptomatic, tested negative, and will undergo a minimum three-week quarantine in a 500-bed facility. The flight crew and passengers will wear full personal protective equipment, and the government states there is no transmission risk. Health Minister Mark Butler emphasized the strict quarantine measures but noted that isolation beyond the initial period may be required due to a potential 42-day incubation period.
